Limits, Widths, Midpoints, and Intervals from Age Group Labels

Source: R/age_lower.R
age_lower.Rd

Calculate lower limits, upper limits, widths, midpoints, and intervals from age group labels.

Usage

age_lower(labels, interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"))

age_mid(labels, interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"))

age_upper(labels, interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"))

age_width(labels, interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"))

age_interval(labels, interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent"))

Arguments

labels

Vector of age group labels.

interpret_fail

Action if element of labels cannot be interpreted. Choices are "error" (the default), "warn", and "silent".

Value

age_interval() returns a character vector, and the other functions return a numeric vector. The result has the same length as labels. If labels has names, the result has the same names.

Details

Lower and upper limits can be used to filter on age. See below for examples.

age_mid() assigns open age groups (e.g., "100+") honorary midpoints, which are useful for plotting. An open age group gets a midpoint half the width of the closed age group with the highest lower limit, so that, for instance, the midpoint of "100+" is 102.5 when the other age groups are five-year groups. If labels has no closed age groups, age_mid() throws an error.

age_interval() describes each age group using interval notation. For instance, "[5, 10)" includes age 5 but not age 10, and "[100, Inf)" has no upper limit. age_interval() is useful for checking how labels are being interpreted.

See also

  • period_lower() Period equivalent of age_lower()

  • cohort_lower() Cohort equivalent of age_lower()

Examples

labels <- c("5-9", "10-14", "100+")
age_lower(labels)
#> [1]   5  10 100
age_upper(labels)
#> [1]  10  15 Inf
age_width(labels)
#> [1]   5   5 Inf
age_mid(labels)
#> [1]   7.5  12.5 102.5
age_interval(labels)
#> [1] "[5, 10)"    "[10, 15)"   "[100, Inf)"

## use 'age_lower()' to filter on age
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
df <- tribble(
  ~age, ~count,
  "5-9", 11,
  "10-14", 20,
  "100+", 7
)
df
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   age   count
#>   <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 5-9      11
#> 2 10-14    20
#> 3 100+      7
df |> filter(age_lower(age) >= 10)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   age   count
#>   <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 10-14    20
#> 2 100+      7

## midpoint of open intervals
age_mid(c("80-89", "90-99", "100+")) # 105
#> [1]  85  95 105
age_mid(c("90-94", "95-99", "100+")) # 102.5
#> [1]  92.5  97.5 102.5

## no action when 'interpret_fail' is "silent"
age_lower(
  labels = c("0-4", "young people", "50plus"),
  interpret_fail = "silent"
)
#> [1]  0 NA 50

## names of 'labels' are kept
pop <- c(young = "0-14", working = "15-64", old = "65+")
age_lower(pop)
#>   young working     old 
#>       0      15      65
